name: Camassia Slopes Preserve
dates: Spring for the wildflowers, access by arrangement
unique: Terraced slopes of high base soil above an old river terrace where a community of plants survives from a colder climate, including wild hyacinth, and the ground tilts between fifteen and thirty five degrees, which is why the woods were never plowed.
buzz: Botanists treat it as a relic and most North Carolinians have never heard of it. Access is limited and arranged in advance, and the spring bloom is the reason to ask.

name: Roanoke River Paddle Trail
unique: A mapped paddling trail down the Roanoke with wooden camping platforms on the bank, through bottomland forest where black bears, river otters and more than two hundred bird species live and the current does most of the work.
buzz: Paddlers plan two and three day trips between the platforms and see bears regularly in early morning. The river is wide, brown and quiet, with no houses on long stretches.

name: Pee Dee National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Eight and a half thousand acres of bottomland hardwood, upland pine and moist soil impoundments along the Pee Dee River, managed for wintering waterfowl with a driving route and blinds drawn by lottery.
buzz: In December the impoundments fill with ducks, geese and swans and the drive is free. Birders work the edges and hunters apply for the draws a year ahead.

name: Blewett Falls Lake
dates: Year round, best spring to fall
company: Duke Energy and the North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission
unique: A narrow reservoir on the Pee Dee below the old Blewett Falls dam, with more than fifty miles of shoreline, cypress and hardwood along the banks and a campground and boat access at the state recreation area.
buzz: Anglers fish it for bass, crappie and catfish and it is quiet because most people drive past it to the bigger lakes. The dam and falls are the historic anchor.

name: Wadesboro Courthouse Square
unique: A square with a 1910s courthouse and a ring of storefronts in a county that grew on cotton and the railroad, in the town where the state's first textile mill village took shape nearby.
buzz: Quiet and easy to walk, with a couple of lunch places that serve the courthouse crowd. People stop on the way to the refuge.

name: Raven Rock State Park
unique: A hundred and fifty foot rock outcrop over the Cape Fear River, with trails down to the base, rapids and Lanier Falls upstream, and a canoe access where the river turns from piedmont to coastal plain.
buzz: The rock and the river view are the payoff and the stairs down are steep. Paddlers use the access for the Cape Fear and hikers do the loop to the falls.

name: Averasboro Battlefield
unique: The ground of the March 1865 battle that delayed Sherman's army for two days on the road to Bentonville, with earthworks, a museum in a small building and a Confederate cemetery on the hill.
buzz: It is small and volunteer run and the museum is only open some days, which people learn to check. The earthworks and the cemetery are the reason to walk it.

name: Dunn Downtown
unique: A railroad town on the Wilmington and Fayetteville line with a restored depot, a main street of brick storefronts and a barbecue tradition that the interstate traffic has kept alive.
buzz: It is a stop on I-95 that people actually get off for. The barbecue places are the reason and the depot is the surprise.

name: Temple Theatre
unique: A 1925 vaudeville and movie house restored as a producing theater, with a full season of musicals and plays built in house, ornate plaster work and a balcony, in a town that has made the theater its civic project.
buzz: The productions are professional and the building is beautiful, which is not what people expect from a Sandhills mill town. Locals buy season tickets.

name: Sanford Historic District
unique: A downtown of 1900s brick commercial buildings with a railroad running through it, in a town that grew on brick, textiles and the railroad and has kept a working main street.
buzz: The district is walkable and the restaurants are local. People arrive for a show and walk the block before curtain.

name: Deep River
unique: A piedmont river running through Sanford with rocky shoals, a couple of public accesses and enough current to make a float interesting without being dangerous.
buzz: Locals float it in spring and fish the pools for bass. It is not a managed park, so bring two cars and expect to carry around the shoals.

name: House in the Horseshoe
unique: A 1772 plantation house inside a horseshoe bend of the Deep River with bullet holes still in the walls from a 1781 raid by Loyalists, plus the family's later years and the enslaved people who worked the land.
buzz: The bullet holes in the clapboard are what everybody looks for, and the rangers point them out. The river bend is beautiful and the drive in is a back road.

name: Weymouth Woods Sandhills Nature Preserve
unique: Nine hundred acres of longleaf pine and wiregrass sandhills with a nature center, a boardwalk and trails to the oldest known living longleaf pine in the state, a tree that was a sapling before Columbus.
buzz: The old growth longleaf is the thing people come to see and the red cockaded woodpecker is the thing birders come for. The trails are flat and sandy and easy in winter.

name: Pinehurst No. 2
dates: Year round, resort guest and package priority
unique: Donald Ross's 1907 course with the crowned greens and sandy waste areas restored in 2010 to how they looked in the 1940s, host of three US Opens and the anchor of a resort that invented the American golf vacation.
buzz: Golfers describe the greens as the hardest they have played and the restoration as the best thing the resort ever did. Non golfers come for the spa and the village.

name: Carthage Courthouse Square
unique: A square with an 1920s courthouse on a rise, a ring of brick storefronts and a monument, in the county seat that predates the golf resorts by a century.
buzz: It is the old Moore County that the Pinehurst crowd rarely sees, quiet and cheap, with a cafe and an antiques shop.

name: Bentonville Battlefield
dates: Grounds daily, visitor center Tuesday to Saturday
customer: Civil War travellers, families, school groups
unique: The ground of the largest battle ever fought in North Carolina, in March 1865, where Sherman's army and Johnston's last Confederate force fought to a standstill over three days, with reconstructed earthworks, a visitor center and a driving tour.
buzz: The scale is bigger than people expect and the earthworks are intact in the woods. Reenactments every five years draw tens of thousands and the driving tour takes an hour.

name: Ava Gardner Museum
unique: The largest collection of Ava Gardner material anywhere, in the town where the actress was born, with costumes, posters, photographs and the gowns and jewelry of a movie star who left Smithfield for Hollywood and never pretended otherwise.
buzz: Film buffs make the trip and locals are proud of her. The dresses and the studio portraits are the parts people linger over.

name: Smithfield Downtown
unique: A river town on the Neuse with a brick main street, a 1920s theater and restaurants that have been serving eastern Carolina barbecue and country cooking for generations.
buzz: The barbecue is the point and the town knows it. People stop on the way to the beach and end up eating in Smithfield instead of on the highway.

name: Howell Woods Environmental Learning Center
unique: Nearly three thousand acres of bottomland, pine and managed wildlife habitat run by the community college, with trails, a learning center and one of the best bird lists in the piedmont.
buzz: Birders know it and most other people do not, which keeps it quiet. The trails are flat and the center runs programs for schools.

name: Fort Branch
unique: Confederate earthworks on a hundred foot bluff above the Roanoke, built to keep Union gunboats from the railroad bridge upstream, with the original cannon positions and a view over a bend in the river.
buzz: The bluff and the earthworks are remarkably intact and the volunteers who open it know the engineering. It is quiet and you can see why the site was chosen.

name: Williamston Downtown
unique: A main street of brick storefronts a few blocks from the Roanoke, with a courthouse, a theater and the peanut and tobacco economy of the inner coastal plain around it.
buzz: The town is small and the river is close. People stop for lunch on the way to the fort or the boat ramp.

name: Soul City
unique: The site of a planned city founded in 1969 by the civil rights lawyer Floyd McKissick to build Black economic power in rural North Carolina, with the shell of the health care building, a water tower, a few houses and a lot of empty lots where the rest was supposed to go.
buzz: People come to see a dream that ran out of federal money and find a handful of residents still living there. The marker and the scale of the site are the story.

name: Warrenton Historic District
unique: A grid of streets with one of the finest collections of antebellum and Victorian houses in the state, a 1900s courthouse and a main street of small shops, in a county that was once the richest in North Carolina and is now one of the poorest.
buzz: Architectural historians rank the district highly and the town is quiet enough to walk alone. The contrast between the houses and the empty storefronts is part of what people notice.

name: Lake Gaston
dates: Year round, best May to October
unique: Twenty thousand acres of water on the Roanoke with three hundred and fifty miles of shoreline, a lake built for pontoon boats and swimming, with rental houses on the coves and marinas on both the North Carolina and Virginia sides.
buzz: Families rent a house for a week and never leave the water. Anglers fish the brush for largemouth and the lake is big enough to ski on the main channel.
